proposed_convention_rulings.proposed_rule: A status letter written per listed item in a register's Status column is a review code for the listed item, not a decision printed for the register page. Record it as decision state present with the letter as literal and the class from the legend of the same package (cover form or title-block A-E block), actor 'consultant' with actor_state inferred (unless a name, stamp or signature on that page identifies who entered it, then resolved), location outside_title_block, association uncertain with an association_note stating the rows covered (all rows / some rows blank). Such a row never counts toward carries_fact. If letters on different rows differ, state ambiguous. A register whose Status column is empty is absent with blank_decision_area. The document decision is resolved, or not, by the cover form and the sheet title blocks; uncertain register letters neither add nor block it.

proposed_convention_rulings.topic: (g) revision appended to the reference with its own 'Rev.' label
proposed_convention_rulings.proposed_rule: Distinguish a labelled revision tail from an unlabelled suffix. Where the reference prints '<number>-Rev.<value>' (the token 'Rev.' is itself a label), record identity as the number without the tail and revision as <value> with printed_label 'Rev. (in ...)', semantic_role 'labelled revision appended to the reference', association resolved. Keep the conventions' suffix rule (semantic_role 'suffix of the printed document number', association uncertain) for unlabelled tails such as '-R00' or '_B'. A scorer should accept either the bare number or the full printed string with the tail as the identity on such pages, and the drafted literal should note the full printed string.
proposed_convention_rulings.evidence: All six registers print 'Submittal Ref: B01-ASC-SD-ELE-0xxx-Rev.00'; each matching cover prints the same number in 'Submittal Ref.No.' with a separate 'Rev. No.' cell (0 or 00).
